To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

quinone redness cycling does not appear to be an essential requirement for tumor promotion and that the tumor promoting activity of juglone, a relatively poor redox cycling agent, may be related to the ability of this agent to produce a pro-oxidation state in the skin.

the tumor promoting activity of quinones is related to their ability to induce ODC in the epidermis and that the quinones that are the most effective tumor promoters are those that induce epidermal hyperplasia and hyperkeratosis, as well as ODC activity.

the ability of structually related quinones and anthrones to promote papilloma formation correlates with their ability to induce ODC, and that the ability to undergo redox cycling does not correlate with tumor promotion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a predictive in vitro test to assess the tumor promoting potential of a chemical.
the identification of the molecular events involved in the initiation and promotion phases of skin tumorigenesis.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of tumor promoters and the development of new tumor promoters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
quinones are not effective tumor promoters.
the ability of quinones to promote papilloma formation correlates with their ability to induce ODC in mouse skin, and that this relationship is independent of the ability to redox cycle.
the ability of a compound to promote tumor formation in mouse skin is not dependent upon its ability to undergo redox cycling, but is dependent upon the ability to induce ODC in mouse epidermis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the induction of epidermal O DC is a useful and sensitive marker for tumor promotion and that the induction of ODC may be mediated by the generation of reactive oxygen intermediates.
the ability of quinones to promote papilloma formation is dependent upon the ability of these compounds to induce epidermis ornithine decarbosylase.
quinones, like anthrones, can be tumor promoters and that this activity is dependent upon the ability to induce ODC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor promoting activity of the structurally related quinine group of compounds is related to their ability to induce epdimermal ODC activity.
the ability of a compound to induce epidermis ornithine decarbosylase activity is a very good predictor of its tumor promoting activity.
quinones can be tumor promoters, but the relationship to their ability to undergo redox cycling and the induction of epidermal OOC is not clear.
